Reference grid

Precision hexes (blue) show the H3 grid at a finer resolution for your current view — zoom in for more detail. Turning the option above on limits them to only your maximum zoom level, so they don't clutter zoomed-out views.

Resolution 1 hexes (violet) show the 842 top-level H3 cells worldwide. Mousing over one shows its raw H3 cell index (e.g. 81a8fffffffffff) and/or its curated 3-word name, depending on which options above are on. "Show 3 word names" also labels Precision hexes on hover with their derived 3-word address.

Thunderforest API key

The Street and Terrain map layers need a free API key from thunderforest.com (their free "Hobby Project" tier covers this while it's in development). Without a key, tiles will show a "API Key Required" watermark.

Thunderforest key saved

OpenWeatherMap API

Clouds & temperature (in the main tab's Live weather section) and forecasts need a free API key from openweathermap.org specifically — other weather services' keys (e.g. WeatherAPI.com) won't work here.

OpenWeatherMap key saved

Gemini API

A.I. Story (Waypoints tab → Trip folders) needs a free API key from Google AI Studio. Google's free tier has no ongoing cost, but is rate-limited and may use your prompts to improve their products.

Gemini key saved

Story Narration

On by default for a natural A.I. voice — needs your Gemini key above (free tier works) and takes a few seconds to generate each time. Turn this off to use your device's own voice instead (free, instant, no setup).

Import waypoints

Imports one waypoint per record from a plain .txt file, all marked with the ⛺ tent emoji. Each record is 7 lines, in this exact order, with a line containing just --- between records:

  1. Waypoint name
  2. Picture (a full image URL, or leave the line blank)
  3. Access type (e.g. Drive in site, Boat Access Only)
  4. Description
  5. Coordinates (e.g. 45.11824 °N - 76.99567 °W)
  6. What3Words location
  7. Amenities, comma-separated (e.g. Fire Pit, Privy)

Any optional line can be left blank, but all 7 lines must be present for each record.

Drag & drop a .txt file, or click to choose one

Import waypoints from CSV

Imports one waypoint per row from a plain .csv file, all marked with the ⛺ tent emoji. The first row is treated as a header and skipped -- every row after it needs 10 columns, one per field below. Drag a field up or down to match the order your CSV's columns are actually in:

    Only Waypoint Name, Latitude, and Longitude are required -- the rest can be left blank, but every column must still have its place (use a trailing comma to leave one empty). For Images, separate more than one URL within the same cell with a | (pipe) character.

    Drag & drop a .csv file, or click to choose one

    Import waypoints from GPX

    Imports every <wpt> waypoint from a standard .gpx file (exported by most GPS devices and apps -- Garmin, Gaia GPS, CalTopo, and others), all marked with the ⛺ tent emoji. Reads each waypoint's name, description/comment, elevation, and link if present -- tracks and routes in the file are not imported, only individual waypoints.

    Drag & drop a .gpx file, or click to choose one

    Import waypoints from KML

    Imports every point <Placemark> from a standard .kml file (exported by Google Earth, Google My Maps, and most GIS software), all marked with the ⛺ tent emoji. Reads each point's name and description -- paths and polygons in the file are not imported, only individual points.

    Drag & drop a .kml file, or click to choose one

    Import waypoints from KMZ

    Imports every point <Placemark> from a compressed .kmz file (Google Earth's zipped KML format), all marked with the ⛺ tent emoji. Reads each point's name and description -- paths and polygons in the file are not imported, only individual points.

    Drag & drop a .kmz file, or click to choose one

    Import waypoints from GeoJSON

    Imports every Point feature from a standard .geojson file (used by Leaflet, Mapbox, OpenLayers, and most modern web mapping tools), all marked with the ⛺ tent emoji. Reads each point's name property plus any others as notes -- lines and polygons in the file are not imported, only individual points.

    Drag & drop a .geojson file, or click to choose one

    Import waypoints from FIT

    Imports named course points from a .fit file (Garmin's binary GPS/fitness format), all marked with the ⛺ tent emoji. If the file has no named course points -- common for a plain recorded activity rather than a planned course -- its starting location is imported instead.

    Drag & drop a .fit file, or click to choose one

    Import waypoints from Shapefile (SHP)

    Imports point features from an ESRI Shapefile, all marked with the ⛺ tent emoji. For names and other attributes, upload a .zip containing the full set (.shp, .dbf, and ideally .prj) -- a bare .shp alone has coordinates but no names, since those live in the companion .dbf file.

    Drag & drop a .zip or .shp file, or click to choose one

    Download map tiles

    Map styles to download

    Zoom range

    Lower = zoomed out (whole area at once), higher = zoomed in (street-level detail). Each extra level roughly quadruples the tile count, so a wide range at high detail can get large fast.

    The number of place names saved depends on the area. A city gets every street name saved, and a region will get main roads saved. A very large area gets towns only, and anything larger than that, the names are not saved.

    Downloading map tiles…

    Downloading slowly on purpose, so this doesn't look like a burst of automated traffic to the map provider — a large area can genuinely take a while.

    Preview: what will actually download

    Map tiles are square, so the real download (solid amber squares) won't exactly match the shape you drew (dashed cyan outline) — edge tiles get included or left out based on whether their center falls inside your shape. You can drag the white dots on the map right now to adjust the shape if the coverage isn't quite right.
